title: Average restriction covariance and projection covariance
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability distribution $\pi$, and let $I$ be a finite nonempty index set with a distinguished orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ for the $\pi$-weighted inner product, one basis vector being the constant function $1$. For any natural number $n$, functions $f,g:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and coordinate $j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the average over independent $\pi$-distributed values $\omega,\omega'$ of the product-space covariance of $f$ and $g$ after replacing coordinate $j$ by $\omega$ and $\omega'$, respectively, equals the product-space covariance of their projections obtained by averaging over all coordinates except $j$.
hypotheses_covered: $I$ is finite and nonempty with decidable equality
A real basis of functions on $\Omega$ indexed by $I$ exists
The distinguished basis vector is constant $1$
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
$j$ is a coordinate among the $n$ coordinates
